group_assessment.weighting: A paediatric-neurology and neuroradiology group (IRCCS Gaslini, Genoa) writing a literature mini-review whose declared subject is the radiological spectrum of WOREE. It contributes NO new cohort: every count in its Table 1 is carried from the studies it collates, so it is a denominator instrument and never a primary measurement. Read under that limit.
group_assessment.counts_measured: Not a per-author sweep: this record's weighting rests on the article's own declaration that it contributes no new cohort. publications_on_gene is 1 — this mini-review — for the group as it appears on this paper.

field_density.note: The density measurement is itself the point: ONE PubMed record ties WWOX to the phrase 'cerebellar vermis', which is why a 'described in most cases' frequency could never have rested on a measured denominator.

multihop.reason: Deliberately not performed. This event verifies three strings inside one collation; its references are the studies the collation counts, and following them would be a different reading with its own coverage map. The one reference this reading needed to attribute correctly — the five-patient cohort whose cerebellum was unaffected — is resolved inside the body text itself and is recorded as a locator. The 35 gene-direct references are enumerated and recorded as queued debt rather than resolved; none is claimed as read by this event.
multihop.enumeration_method: Counted mechanically on the fingerprinted JATS XML: 70 <ref> elements, all 70 carrying a PubMed identifier. Gene-direct = reference text naming WWOX/Wwox/WOX1/FRA16D/16q23, matched over the de-marked reference text: 35 of 70.

entries.proposition: THE DENOMINATOR THE LEDGER'S 'most cases' NEVER HAD: in the only literature collation whose declared subject is the WOREE radiological spectrum, cerebellar vermis hypoplasia is recorded as 2:2 in Table 1 against a total of 101 collated patients. The 2:2 is one study's own count, not a rate over the collation.
entries.anchor: Table 1, 'Hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis' row; the table's last row reads 'Total number of patients 101' and its footnote reads '+, number of patients unspecified'

entries.proposition: THE REVIEW ITSELF PLACES VERMIS HYPOPLASIA AMONG THE LESS SPECIFIC, LOWER-FREQUENCY FINDINGS — the opposite of 'described in most cases'.
entries.snippet: cerebellar vermis hypoplasia were observed in a lower percentage of cases, and therefore these findings seem to be less specific
entries.anchor: Results, closing sentence of the imaging-frequency paragraph, immediately before the Discussion

entries.proposition: A FIVE-PATIENT COHORT IN WHICH THE CEREBELLUM WAS EXPLICITLY UNAFFECTED, attributed here first-hand: the sentence belongs to the Tabarki cohort of five patients from two unrelated families carrying the same homozygous WWOX variant, reference 51 of this review.
entries.snippet: Of note, the cerebellum was not affected
entries.anchor: Results, narrative of the collated studies, the sentence closing the Tabarki et al. paragraph ('five patients from two unrelated families'), citing reference 51

entries.proposition: WHAT THE REVIEW DOES CALL PREDOMINANT, so that the correction removes a frequency without removing the finding: corpus callosum hypoplasia and brain atrophy, not cerebellar vermis hypoplasia.
entries.snippet: hypoplasia of the corpus callosum and brain atrophy appeared to be the predominant MRI alterations
entries.anchor: Discussion, sentence following 'This review analyzed 101 cases of children with various mutations in the WWOX gene associated with WOREE syndrome from 2014 to 2023'

entries.proposition: Table 1's total of 101 is a sum over overlapping sources; the Clinical section of the same paper counts 84 reported patients.
entries.snippet: 84 patients have been reported in the literature with descriptions of the individual phenotypes
This review analyzed 101 cases of children with various mutations in the WWOX gene associated with WOREE syndrome from 2014 to 2023.

entries.proposition: Banne 2021, one of the summed sources, is itself a collation of 56 published cases.
entries.snippet: Similar features were found in 2021 by Banne et al., who retrospectively analyzed 45 variants in 56 WOREE published cases.

entries.proposition: Piard: abnormal MRI in 80% — so not all patients have MRI anomalies.
entries.snippet: The study detected abnormal brain MRI in 80% of them

entries.proposition: The 13% progression figure is computed over all 101, including patients never re-imaged.
entries.snippet: approximately 13% of the patients included in the study also demonstrated age-related progression

entries.proposition: In Oliver, 7 of 13 had serial MRI, and those showed progression.
entries.snippet: Lastly, 7 of 13 patients underwent serial MRI, which showed progression of the abnormalities with age

entries.proposition: The Q230P eight-case count is the review's citation of reference 1, not its own count.
entries.snippet: has been described both in homozygosity and in compound heterozygosity in eight cases overall

entries.proposition: The MS variant count is cited to a C6orf10 study.
entries.snippet: WWOX has been identified as a susceptible gene in MS and 48 WWOX pathogenic variants have been detected in affected patients

entries.proposition: Figure 1 re-uses one child and one fetus from Iacomino 2020.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1: A' sagittal T1 with open arrow on thin corpus callosum and arrowhead on inferior vermis; A'' axial T2 with arrows on white matter; B' fetal and B'' post-mortem sagittal MRI with black arrows on the vermis. Legend ends 'Courtesy of Prof. Salpietro (50)'.

entries.proposition: The Discussion (and the abstract) claim MRI anomalies in all patients.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, all affected patients presented brain anomalies at MRI
